{{Short description|Type of functions in algebra}}
{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In [[Abstract algebra|algebra]], a '''polynomial map''' or '''polynomial mapping''' <math>P: V \to W</math> between [[vector space]]s over an infinite [[Field (mathematics)|field]] ''k'' is a [[polynomial]] in [[linear functional]]s with coefficients in ''k''; i.e., it can be written as
<math display="block">P(v) = \sum_{i_1, \dots, i_n} \lambda_{i_1}(v) \cdots \lambda_{i_n}(v) w_{i_1, \dots, i_n}</math>
where the <math>\lambda_{i_j}: V \to k</math> are linear functionals and the <math>w_{i_1, \dots, i_n}</math> are vectors in ''W''. For example, if <math>W = k^m</math>, then a polynomial mapping can be expressed as <math>P(v) = (P_1(v), \dots, P_m(v))</math> where the <math>P_i</math> are (scalar-valued) [[polynomial function]]s on ''V''. (The abstract definition has an advantage that the map is manifestly free of a choice of basis.)

When ''V'', ''W'' are [[Dimension (vector space)|finite-dimensional]] vector spaces and are viewed as [[algebraic varieties]], then a polynomial mapping is precisely a [[morphism of algebraic varieties]].
